name: South Carolina
summary: Statutes, constitution, regulations and the State Register all come from scstatehouse.gov (unofficial, robots-permitted, script and fetch tool both work): the Code is one HTML page per chapter (t{TT}c{CCC}.php, no section anchors, long chapters truncate in the fetch tool) current through the 2025 Session; the Constitution is per-article PDFs; regulations are chapter PDFs (some 1.5M chars). The judiciary site www.sccourts.org disallows all robots, so official opinions and ALL court rules (SCRCP, SCRE, SCACR/RPC) are link-only with no tier-2 copy of the rules. Case text comes from Justia (constructible by Opinion No., incl. unpublished YYYY-UP-NNN; fetch tool only, script refused); subsequent history (docket events only) from the court's robots-free C-Track docket portal by a plain GET search. State Library depository advance sheets are tier 1 but link-only (PDFs 403).

citation_map.notes: The statute URL needs no code key: title and chapter come straight from 'T-C-S' (pad title to 2, chapter to 3 digits). law_aliases map act names to their title or title-chapter so a named act can be routed to the chapter page. Bare '§ 15-3-530' / 'Section 15-3-530' is shared in form with other three-part codes (Tennessee, Georgia, Indiana, etc.) and is context_required. SC rule cites put the rule set AFTER the number ('Rule 12(b)(6), SCRCP'; RPC as 'Rule 8.4(e), RPC, Rule 407, SCACR'); bare 'Rule 12(b)(6)' or 'Rules of Civil Procedure' route here only with S.C. context. The '(?<![\w.])' guard keeps '42 U.S.C. 1983' from reading as an S.C. Reports cite. S.C. has no public-domain citation; the court's Opinion No. (5-digit Supreme Court, 4-digit published COA) and 'YYYY-UP-NNN' (unpublished COA) / 'YYYY-MO-NNN' (Supreme Court memorandum) numbers are the opinion keys and also the Justia URL key. Unpublished opinions have no precedential value (Rule 268(d)(2), SCACR). Advance-sheet cites ('Howard Adv. Sh.', earlier 'Shearouse'/'Davis') are pre-reporter cites. The Appellate Case No. 'YYYY-NNNNNN' is the docket key for C-Track. Cert dispositions (S.C. Supreme Court cert to the COA, and U.S. Supreme Court notices) are found on the C-Track docket; from a COA decision search the Supreme Court by party name. CourtListener ids from memory, unverified.

sources.publisher: South Carolina Legislative Council / Legislative Services Agency
sources.official_status_evidence: https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/statmast.php DISCLAIMER: this version 'is not official'; only the published volumes of the S.C. Code of Laws Annotated and the acts are official.
sources.coverage: All 63 titles, one HTML page per chapter (text, numbering, history, editor's notes); per-chapter Word downloads. Historical snapshots under /Archives/CodeofLaws{YYYY}/ (seen in search results for 2000-2013, not fetched).

access.pattern_rules: Citation S.C. Code Ann. § {T}-{C}-{S}: title = T zero-padded to 2 digits; chapter = C zero-padded to 3 digits with any letter suffix kept upper-case (15-3-530 -> t15c003.php; 1-23-380 -> t01c023.php; 36-2A-103 -> t36c002A.php). The page holds the WHOLE chapter; there are no section anchors (no id/name attributes), so locate the section by the literal text 'SECTION {T}-{C}-{S}.' (script: fetch_doc.py grep/section). Chapters ending 'R' (t40c021R.php) are RESERVED stubs. Word file of a chapter: /getfile.php?TYPE=CODEOFLAWS&TITLE={T}&CHAPTER={C} (unpadded). Title index /code/title{T}.php (unpadded) lists chapter names only, no section ranges; not needed because the chapter is in the citation.

automation.notes: WebFetch read built URLs on this host without an approval prompt. Long chapters exceed the WebFetch window: t16c003.php is 124,663 chars of text and WebFetch stopped inside § 16-3-740 (continue with offset 100000). Script sizes (raw text incl. whitespace): t15c003 45,604; t01c023 140,304; t16c003 333,507; t63c007 314,879; t12c006 508,386 chars. Prefer fetch_doc.py grep/section on long chapters. Full-text search (query.php) needs a JavaScript auto-submit; a hand-built GET returned 'found 0 times'/'Submitting...' - not usable.
